newsitem.title: USA: Republican calls for balanced budget amendment.
newsitem.headline: Republican calls for balanced budget amendment.

text.p: A senior Republican senator said Saturday the only way to make the president and Congress balance the federal budget was with the force of a constitutional amendment.

"Without the force of a balanced-budget amendment, a federal budget that stays balanced isn't possible," Larry Craig of Idaho said in the Republican response to President Clinton's weekly radio address.
"Without the force of a constitutional amendment, Congress and the executive branch will not make the tough choices necessary (to balance the budget)," Craig said.

The Senate is scheduled to vote Tuesday on a proposed constitutional amendment requiring an annual balanced budget, but supporters appear to be one vote short of the 67 senators needed for the two-thirds majority required for passage.
The House would also have to pass the amendment by a two-thirds majority to send it to the states for ratification.
Clinton opposes the constitutional amendment but says he will work with the Republican-controlled Congress to pass a balanced budget.

Craig said passage of a balanced budget amendment was the best way to protect the financial soundness of the Social Security system. He said Congress owed it to the American people, especially children, senior citizens and the disadvantaged, to pass the amendment.
